parts.label: a
parts.ask: A balloon is modelled as a sphere whose radius \(r\) cm increases at a rate inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{r}\). Write down a differential equation for this.
parts.method: Turn the words into an equation

steps.text: "The rate of increase of the radius" is \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t}\). "Inversely proportional to \(\sqrt{r}\)" means a constant divided by \(\sqrt{r}\).
steps.why: Proportional always needs a constant, \(k\). Without it the model is wrong.

slips: Writing \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r}}\), with no constant. That also capped the marks in (b).

check.answers: a model written from words: no number to compare

parts.label: b
parts.ask: At \(t = 10\) the radius is 16 cm and is increasing at 0.9 cm s⁻¹. Solve the differential equation to show that \(r^{\frac{3}{2}} = 5.4t + 10\).
parts.method: Find \(k\) first, then separate the variables

steps.why: Put \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.9\) and \(r = 16\) into the model. Finding \(k\) now leaves only one unknown, \(c\), later.
Multiply both sides by \(\sqrt{r}\), so all the \(r\) terms are on one side.

slips: Getting the power of \(r\) wrong, from a wrong model or from separating the variables wrongly.
Not finding \(k\) at the start, then being stuck with both \(k\) and \(c\) unknown.
Putting 0.9 in for \(k\) instead of for \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

parts.label: c
parts.ask: Hence find the radius when \(t = 20\), to the nearest millimetre.

steps.why: Raise both sides to the power \(\tfrac{2}{3}\): \(\left(r^{\frac{3}{2}}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}} = r\).

steps.text: The nearest millimetre is 1 decimal place in centimetres.

slips: Undoing the power wrongly, for example working out \(118^{\frac{3}{2}}\) instead of \(118^{\frac{2}{3}}\).
Leaving out the units, or a slip converting to millimetres.

parts.label: d
parts.ask: Suggest a limitation of the model.
parts.method: Think about what happens to a real balloon

steps.text: The model lets \(r\) grow for ever: \(r^{\frac{3}{2}} = 5.4t + 10\) has no upper limit.

parts.answerText: A real balloon will burst, so the model cannot hold for large \(t\). (A balloon is also not a perfect sphere.)
slips: Saying the rate of inflation is not constant. The model already has a changing rate, so this doesn't count.

check.answers: a comment on the model: no number to compare
